arguments:
const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: D:\Program\python\Dubbed\_docs\frontend-flows\10-result.md
+# Flow 10 — Result assembly, playback and download
+
+Date: 2026-10-22 (Asia/Qyzylorda).
+Status: initial specification draft; three owner decisions are pending through the Orchestrator and are listed under **Open decisions**.
+Mode: specification only. No implementation, mock, rendered design, visual validation or executed test is represented by this document.
+
+## 1. Purpose and authority
+
+This flow lets an authenticated project owner see result assembly start after the last required take is durably accepted, follow truthful progress, watch the latest valid finished dub, download its MP4, open the sharing controls, and return to the project's turns.
+
+The [shared frontend contract](00-shared-contract.md) governs the shell, current light visual direction, localization, service boundary and cross-flow behavior. Its latest owner decisions override conflicting older wording in BR-001 and SPEC-001. The Result flow therefore uses the compact top navigation and Prepare / Record / Result workspace with no permanent sidebar, white or light-gray working surfaces, a black video stage and no gradients or decorative effects.
+
+Unchanged output invariants come from BR-001-R14–R18 and SPEC-001 §§4.5, 5, 7–9, AC-11–AC-17 and AC-23. Every nonempty prepared turn must have a compatible durable accepted take before a new result can be assembled. A shorter accepted take remains valid. A timing edit invalidates the affected take for output; a text-only or speaker-label-only edit does not. The output is MP4 up to 720p, preserves the selected section's orientation, never upscales, adds no subtitles, and keeps burned-in source captions unchanged.
+
+This document applies both requested design skills as analysis guidance:
+
+- `design-taste-frontend` is applied as an **app-screen** workflow: one screen question, restrained chrome, flat surfaces, honest states, a no-sidebar shell and responsive operation rather than a landing-page composition.
+- `frontend-design` is applied through subject-specific hierarchy: the finished moving dub is the distinctive and largest object, while progress, provenance and next actions exist to support it.
+
+No random style draw, token generation, implementation asset or mockup is created. The shared contract already fixes the owner-approved direction, exact visual tokens remain open, and this assignment permits editing only this specification.
+
+## 2. Entry, exit and scope
+
+### Entry
+
+The user enters Result through one of these paths:
+
+1. **Automatic last-take handoff.** Flow 09 durably accepts the final required candidate, confirms that every current turn has a compatible accepted take, and requests result assembly for that authoritative eligibility snapshot.
+2. **Resume.** The user opens Result for a project whose result job is queued, rendering, validating, finished, failed or stale.
+3. **Previous result.** The project has a valid prior finished result while later edits, recording work or a replacement render exist.
+4. **Recovery.** The final take is already accepted, but starting the result job failed or the browser lost the response.
+
+The flow must load authoritative project, eligibility, export-job and finished-generation state before deciding which surface to show. It must not infer completion from client-side turn counts or a locally completed take.
+
+### Successful exit
+
+A successful result state provides:
+
+- full playback of the latest validated finished generation available to the owner;
+- download of that exact generation as an MP4;
+- entry to the separate sharing dialog;
+- an action to return to the project's turns.
+
+The Result screen may remain open while a replacement generation is assembled. A validated completion becomes current only through the generation-ordering rules in §6 and §10.
+
+### Other exits
+
+- Global navigation may leave Result without canceling an authoritative server-side render.
+- Returning to turns hands off to the flow that owns turn navigation and recording. Result does not edit timing, text, speaker labels or takes.
+- Opening sharing hands off to the separate sharing-dialog specification. Opening a public link hands off to the public-viewer specification.
+
+### Out of scope
+
+- preparing, editing, adding or reordering turns;
+- capturing, accepting or replacing takes;
+- a video editor, audio mixer, subtitle editor, performance score or multi-export library;
+- changing resolution, format, orientation, subtitle inclusion, timing or mix parameters;
+- defining the sharing dialog, public viewer, public access policy UI or project deletion confirmation;
+- exposing superseded output generations as a user-managed version history;
+- promising a render duration, automatic retry count, storage lifetime, download limit or hosting limit that has not been approved and evidenced.
+
+## 3. Experience principle and visual hierarchy
+
+The screen's first question is: **Is my dub ready, and what can I do with it?**
+
+When a current finished generation exists, the full video answers that question and is the largest element. During the first assembly, truthful job status occupies the same principal region so the layout does not jump from an unrelated dashboard to a player. During replacement assembly, the treatment of the prior finished player is pending **OPEN-10-02**; the prior generation remains authoritative regardless of its exact presentation.
+
+The visual direction follows the shared light rehearsal room:
+
+- compact top navigation and project header, with Prepare / Record / Result context and authoritative save/job status;
+- no permanent sidebar, hero marketing treatment, KPI row, decorative card grid, gradient, glow or glass;
+- a black media stage against white/light-gray working surfaces;
+- flat action controls, quiet grouping and one filled primary action at most in a state;
+- red only for errors here; recording red does not become general Result decoration;
+- progress uses text and state semantics, never animation or color alone;
+- the exact typeface, colors, radii, measurements, progress treatment and action placement remain shared design decisions rather than defaults introduced by this flow.
+
+Conceptual composition, with no implied measurements:
+
+```text
+Desktop
+┌ compact global navigation ─────────────────────────────────────────┐
+│ project identity · Prepare / Record / Result · authoritative state │
+├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
+│                                                                     │
+│                    black video / result stage                       │
+│             or truthful assembly / recovery surface                 │
+│                                                                     │
+├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
+│ output status or progress                         current duration   │
+│ common playback controls when a valid result exists                 │
+│ Download · Share · Return to turns                                  │
+└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
+
+Phone
+┌ compact top navigation ┐
+│ project + Result state │
+├────────────────────────┤
+│ black media stage      │
+│ or assembly state      │
+├────────────────────────┤
+│ status / progress      │
+│ playback controls      │
+│ primary action         │
+│ other actions          │
+└────────────────────────┘
+```
+
+The wireframes show reading order only. They do not approve exact copy, size, spacing, sticky behavior or button order.
+
+## 4. Screen anatomy
+
+The Result screen contains these semantic regions in reading order.
+
+1. **Shared project shell**
+   - compact global navigation: New dub, My projects, credits balance and account;
+   - project identity and Prepare / Record / Result workspace context;
+   - authoritative project save/result state;
+   - no permanent sidebar.
+2. **Result heading and generation status**
+   - identifies the Result workspace without an oversized landing-page title;
+   - distinguishes `assembling`, `validating`, `ready`, `failed`, `outdated` and `blocked by turns` in plain language;
+   - identifies a previous finished result as previous when current work has not produced a replacement;
+   - does not expose internal worker/provider vocabulary.
+3. **Principal stage**
+   - black media stage preserving the output's orientation without cropping it to a decorative ratio;
+   - shows the latest valid finished generation when that generation is available in the current presentation state;
+   - otherwise keeps the stage footprint while showing assembly, validation, empty or recovery information;
+   - never substitutes the source upload, a sample clip or a partial render for the finished result.
+4. **Assembly progress**
+   - reflects authoritative job state and any backend-supported stage/progress facts;
+   - never invents a percentage, remaining time, stage completion or success from elapsed client time;
+   - reconnecting or refreshing preserves the same operation identity rather than starting duplicate work;
+   - exact stage names, determinate/indeterminate treatment and ETA policy are **OPEN-10-05**.
+5. **Playback controls**
+   - use native or equivalent accessible play/pause, seek, time and volume behavior for the full selected-section output;
+   - operate only on a validated finished asset;
+   - expose no source/take selector and no editing controls;
+   - preserve full selected-section duration, including pauses and scenes outside turns.
+6. **Output facts**
+   - may show only authoritative facts useful to the owner, such as duration and current/previous status;
+   - must not claim 720p when the preserved source is lower resolution, imply upscaling, or describe a sample fixture as the user's render;
+   - exact metadata shown is **OPEN-10-05**.
+7. **Actions**
+   - `Download` requests the exact displayed finished generation;
+   - `Share` opens the separate sharing dialog for the project's current share target;
+   - `Return to turns` exits to the flow that owns the project's turns;
+   - `Retry` exists only in a recoverable failed/start-failed state under the policy selected in **OPEN-10-03**;
+   - unavailable actions remain understandable, with the blocking reason available to keyboard and assistive-technology users.
+8. **Inline status and recovery message**
+   - sits with the failed or blocked region rather than as an unrelated global banner;
+   - says whether a previous result remains safe, whether the accepted takes remain safe, and what action is available;
+   - never describes a worker response as a valid result before media validation and current-generation publication complete.
+
+## 5. State model and transitions
+
+Project edit state, output eligibility, result-job state and current finished generation are independent dimensions. A single `resultStatus` string is insufficient because a project can have a prior finished result, current unrecorded work and a failed replacement job at the same time.
+
+### 5.1 Loading authoritative context
+
+On entry, load:
+
+- project access and deletion state;
+- current preparation/edit and eligibility revisions;
+- turn count and any incompatible/missing accepted-take references;
+- latest requested result operation and its frozen input snapshot;
+- latest valid finished generation and whether it is output-compatible with current project work;
+- sharing-summary state needed only to hand off to the sharing dialog.
+
+Keep the final layout stable while loading. Loading does not start playback, offer download, claim completion or erase an already known valid result. A lost client response must be reconciled by operation identity before another assembly request is created.
+
+### 5.2 Automatic first assembly
+
+After Flow 09 reports durable acceptance of the last required take:
+
+1. Consume the authoritative all-turns-complete eligibility revision returned by the acceptance operation.
+2. Request or reconcile one result operation for that exact eligible snapshot.
+3. Navigate to Result progress without rolling back the accepted take if job creation or navigation fails.
+4. Show queued/rendering/validation progress from server truth.
+5. Validate the finished media and its input provenance.
+6. Atomically make the generation current only if it is still the eligible latest requested generation for the active project.
+7. Replace progress with full playback and enable download/share handoff.
+
+The request is idempotent. Refresh, duplicate `Next`, reconnect or resuming the route cannot create competing billable/publication truth for the same frozen input snapshot.
+
+### 5.3 Replacement after returning to turns
+
+A user can leave a finished result, replace a take, and finish the project's required turns again.
+
+- The prior finished generation remains valid and remains the share target while the replacement is pending, rendering, validating, stale or failed.
+- The replacement job binds immutable source, background, turn, timing and accepted-take revisions.
+- A text-only or speaker-label-only edit does not by itself make a compatible take ineligible. Result compatibility must be evaluated by the authoritative service rather than raw project-revision equality.
+- A timing edit or added turn makes the latest project state ineligible until every affected turn has a compatible accepted take.
+- Once the latest eligible replacement validates and wins the generation fence, it becomes the current owner playback/download target and, when sharing is enabled, the same public link's target.
+- This flow does not promise a user-visible archive of the superseded generation after the atomic switch. Physical retention/cleanup remains governed by the unresolved operational policy in SPEC-001 D08.
+
+The exact on-screen treatment of the prior finished player during replacement progress is **OPEN-10-02**.
+
+### 5.4 Current edits are not eligible
+
+If a project has missing, newly added or timing-invalidated turns:
+
+- do not start or continue a result operation for that ineligible current snapshot;
+- identify that the latest project work needs compatible takes without exposing private transcript content in a global message;
+- keep the prior finished result authoritative when one exists;
+- offer `Return to turns` through the cross-flow handoff;
+- keep Download/Share bound only to the prior finished generation, never to incomplete current work;
+- never fill missing voices with original dialogue or silently use invalidated takes.
+
+Whether `Return to turns` opens Prepare's turn list, Record's first incompatible turn, or another shared destination is **OPEN-10-04** and must be resolved consistently with Flows 08, 09 and 11.
+
+### 5.5 Successful finished state
+
+A generation is ready only after assembly and media validation succeed and publication accepts its generation fence.
+
+- The stage plays the complete selected-section timeline.
+- Download returns the exact displayed generation.
+- Share hands off the project's current finished generation and existing stable-link state.
+- The player does not add app-generated subtitles. Burned-in source captions remain part of source pixels.
+- The UI does not promise a resolution above the actual output or source.
+- Playback failure is distinct from render failure: it does not invalidate the stored generation without authoritative evidence.
+
+### 5.6 First-result failure
+
+If no prior finished result exists and start, render or validation fails:
+
+- keep all accepted takes and project progress intact;
+- show no fake or partial player;
+- disable Download and Share;
+- describe the failed stage only at a user-action level;
+- expose recovery according to **OPEN-10-03**;
+- do not send the user back to recording as though a take had been lost.
+
+### 5.7 Replacement failure with a prior result
+
+If a replacement fails:
+
+- preserve the prior finished generation as current;
+- preserve its existing share target and access state;
+- label the replacement failure separately from the prior result's readiness;
+- never swap a partial, invalid or failed asset into owner playback, download or public sharing;
+- retry only through the selected policy in **OPEN-10-03**.
+
+### 5.8 Stale or out-of-order completion
+
+A completion is stale when its frozen input/request generation is superseded, the project is deleted, current eligibility changed, or a newer accepted result request owns publication priority.
+
+- A stale completion may be recorded for reconciliation but cannot become the current result or share target.
+- Reversed completion order cannot move the project back to older takes.
+- A stale success is not displayed as a successful latest result.
+- If current work is eligible and lacks an active current request, recovery may reconcile or start the correct operation idempotently; it must not reuse incompatible bytes.
+
+### 5.9 Empty and zero-turn states
+
+An empty Result context has no valid finished generation and no active result job.
+
+- If a nonempty project is authoritatively eligible, reconcile the missing assembly-start operation and enter progress.
+- If it is ineligible, show the blocked-by-turns state and hand off to the turn-owning flow.
+- If preparation contains zero turns, behavior is **OPEN-10-01**. The UI must not silently render, offer the source clip as a result, or claim the project is complete until the owner resolves this policy.
+
+### 5.10 Leaving, refresh and cancel semantics
+
+- Refreshing, closing the tab, losing connectivity or using global navigation does not cancel a server-owned result operation.
+- Returning later restores authoritative job and finished-generation state.
+- No result-assembly Cancel control is confirmed. If cancellation is added, what it stops, what happens to a prior result, whether a partial job may finish, and whether any operational limit is consumed require an explicit shared decision under **OPEN-10-05**.
+- A client disconnect is not a render failure, cancellation confirmation or reason to create another job blindly.
+
+## 6. Generation, eligibility and publication invariants
+
+1. **Frozen inputs.** Each result operation references immutable source, selected-section timeline, background, preparation, turn-timing and accepted-take identities.
+2. **All-turn eligibility.** Every turn in a nonempty current preparation must have one compatible durable accepted take. Early-stopped shorter takes remain compatible when accepted under the recording contract.
+3. **Compatibility, not equality.** Text-only and speaker-label-only edits preserve take eligibility. Timing edits and newly added turns require compatible takes. The frontend does not derive this rule from timestamps or compare opaque revision numbers itself.
+4. **One continuous mix.** The full selected-section video and one continuous processed background are combined with accepted takes at their original positions, including overlap and dialogue-free intervals. Do not duplicate per-turn background, time-stretch performances, extend the video or intentionally restore original voices.
+5. **Immutable finished bytes.** Later project edits do not mutate an earlier finished asset. They may change whether it is described as current for the latest work.
+6. **Monotonic publication.** Only the latest eligible requested generation can become current. A late older completion cannot replace it.
+7. **Prior-result protection.** A current finished generation remains owner/download/share truth until a newer eligible generation validates and switches atomically. Failure and stale completion leave it untouched.
+8. **Deletion fence.** A deleted or inaccessible project cannot be revived or republished by a late result completion.
+9. **No fixture confusion.** A fixed sample MP4 used by a frontend mock is not evidence that accepted takes were mixed, that a custom upload rendered, or that production export works.
+
+## 7. Failure and recovery behavior
+
+| Condition | Required Result behavior |
+|---|---|
+| Final take accepted but assembly-start response fails | Keep the take accepted. Reconcile the idempotent start operation; show a recoverable Result state, never a recording rollback. |
+| Job queued/running with lost status connection | Keep last authoritative state, show reconnection status, and poll/subscribe again using the same operation identity. Do not label the job failed from silence alone. |
+| Render worker or storage failure | Preserve accepted takes and the prior finished result. Show a recoverable failure without exposing provider/storage internals. |
+| Output media fails validation | Treat the operation as failed; never enable playback/download/share for that asset. Preserve prior result. |
+| Project or turn revision changes during render | Fence the completion. Do not publish it for the changed project state; return to turns if current work is ineligible. |
+| Older and newer jobs finish in reverse order | Only the publication owner may advance the current generation; the older completion remains stale. |
+| Finished-player network/media error | Keep the generation record intact, retry playback or refresh its secure descriptor. Do not rerender unless authoritative validation says the asset is invalid. |
+| Download request fails or expires | Keep the result ready, report only the download failure and allow a fresh download request for the same generation. |
+| Sharing dialog cannot load | Keep playback/download available; show the dialog failure within the sharing owner surface and allow retry there. |
+| Authentication expires | Preserve server-side work, require reauthentication for owner actions, then restore the same project/result context if authorized. |
+| Project becomes deleted/inaccessible | Stop owner playback/actions and follow project deletion/access behavior. Late job completion cannot restore access. |
+| Browser closes or phone suspends | Server-side assembly may continue. On return, restore job or finished state from the service. |
+
+Failures must say which user-owned work remains safe. They must not claim that an upload, accepted take, render, download or share action succeeded solely because a local animation completed.
+
+## 8. Download contract
+
+`Download` is available only for a validated finished generation that the current account may access.
+
+- Request the exact generation shown in the player, not an unfenced “latest file” URL cached before state refresh.
+- The delivered artifact is MP4, no more than 720p, with source orientation preserved and no upscaling.
+- The selected-section duration and timeline remain intact. No app-generated subtitle track or burn-in is added.
+- A generated filename, expiry duration, download count/traffic limit and offline-retention promise are not selected in this flow.
+- A failed download does not invalidate the generation or start a new render.
+- Signed or private media descriptors must not be exposed in public logs, analytics, error copy or the sharing dialog contract.
+
+Actual export-byte verification requires a real media pipeline. A browser download of a bundled fixture proves only the download UI and transport adapter used in that test.
+
+## 9. Sharing and public-viewer handoff
+
+Result owns only the entry point and the current finished-generation context. It does not duplicate the sharing dialog or public viewer.
+
+### Sharing-dialog handoff
+
+**Input:** authorized project identity, current finished generation identity, and authoritative sharing summary.
+
+**Expected responsibility of the separate dialog:** access on/off, same-token re-enable, copy link and open public viewer. It must keep the prior share target while replacement assembly is pending or failed and switch only after a valid current generation is published.
+
+**Return to Result:** updated access summary or a scoped load/update error. Closing the dialog changes no result-generation state.
+
+### Public-viewer handoff
+
+The public viewer receives only the unlisted capability and resolves the current allowed finished output. It receives no owner session requirement, editing access, source upload, transcript, turns, takes, billing or project-navigation context.
+
+The Result player and public viewer may use the same finished asset identity but are separate authorization surfaces. Their exact layouts and public unavailable/revoked/deleted states belong to their owning specifications.
+
+## 10. Logical service contract
+
+The frontend uses the centralized interchangeable services facade. Names below describe responsibilities, not endpoints, stores or implementation modules.
+
+### Load Result context
+
+**Input:** account/session context and project ID.
+
+**Result:** authorized project summary; current preparation/edit and eligibility revision; turn count; authoritative eligibility state and reason category; current result request/job identity and state; latest valid finished generation; compatibility/current/previous designation; output metadata; sharing summary safe for owner UI; deletion/access state.
+
+**Errors:** unauthorized/not found/deleted, project not prepared, temporary service failure, inconsistent state requiring reconciliation.
+
+### Ensure result assembly
+
+**Input:** project ID; authoritative eligible snapshot identity; frozen source/background/turn/take mapping reference; expected latest request/publication generation; idempotency identity.
+
+**Success:** existing or newly created result operation identity, frozen-input provenance and authoritative initial job state.
+
+**Errors:** zero-turn policy unresolved, incomplete/incompatible takes, stale eligibility/request revision, missing asset, deleted/inaccessible project, operation creation failure, service unavailable.
+
+This command cannot repair, accept or choose takes. It cannot replace a previous finished generation at request time.
+
+### Observe result operation
+
+**Input:** project ID and result operation identity.
+
+**Events/result:** queued/rendering/validating/finished/failed/stale state; authoritative progress facts when supported; recoverability category; finished generation identity only after validation/publication disposition.
+
+**Errors:** unauthorized, unknown operation, temporary connection failure. A missing update is not success or failure.
+
+### Load finished playback
+
+**Input:** project ID and exact finished generation identity.
+
+**Result:** authorized playable descriptor, duration, dimensions/orientation, actual output resolution and media validation identity.
+
+**Errors:** unauthorized, revoked/deleted/unavailable asset, expired descriptor, temporary delivery failure, invalid media. Expired delivery credentials may be refreshed without rerendering.
+
+### Request result download
+
+**Input:** project ID and exact finished generation identity.
+
+**Result:** authorized download descriptor and truthful metadata for that generation.
+
+**Errors:** unauthorized, generation unavailable, expired descriptor, temporary delivery failure. Retrying download targets the same generation.
+
+### Retry result assembly
+
+This is either a new authorized attempt referencing the current eligible snapshot or reconciliation of an uncertain existing attempt. Inputs and result mirror `Ensure result assembly`; policy for automatic versus explicit retry is **OPEN-10-03**. Retry cannot overwrite a prior finished generation before a newer result validates and wins publication.
+
+### Open sharing controls
+
+Flow composition passes project/current-generation context to the sharing-dialog owner. Result must not call public-access mutations directly from unrelated player controls or duplicate stable-link logic in local component state.
+
+## 11. Persistence, ownership and concurrency
+
+- The backend/export boundary is authoritative for result-job state, frozen input provenance, media validation and current-generation publication.
+- Result UI state may cache presentation details but cannot decide eligibility, current generation or share target from local turn arrays.
+- A finished generation is immutable. The project stores a current finished-generation association separately from the latest job and latest edit revision.
+- The previous current generation remains associated while a replacement is pending or failed. Its post-success physical retention is an operational policy, not a visible version-library promise.
+- Duplicate starts and retries use stable operation/idempotency identities. A timeout is reconciled before a new operation is issued.
+- Out-of-order completions, stale edits, account/session changes and project deletion are checked before publication.
+- Download and owner playback are authorized account actions; public playback uses only the share capability.
+- Sharing on/off does not delete or rerender the owner result. Project deletion makes the owner result and link inaccessible according to the project/deletion contracts.
+- Returning to turns does not cancel assembly or mutate a finished generation.
+
+### Ownership boundary with turn flows
+
+Prepare/Record own turn content, timing, accepted-take persistence and the action that makes current work eligible. Result consumes only the authoritative eligibility snapshot and reason categories. It may point the user back to the relevant flow, but it must not:
+
+- mark a take compatible;
+- select a replacement take;
+- undo a timing edit;
+- choose an original-voice fallback;
+- silently assemble an older eligible snapshot as though it represented current work.
+
+Flow 11 My projects may summarize result state, but Result and the export/publication service remain the detailed owner surface and truth for generation progress.
+
+## 12. Desktop, phone and input behavior
+
+### Desktop
+
+- The black video/result stage is the largest region when a finished result is available.
+- Progress/recovery occupies that principal region during a first assembly so the later player does not cause a major layout jump.
+- Result actions remain near the stage and status they affect; they do not become a detached dashboard toolbar.
+- The layout uses the available canvas without a permanent sidebar or a narrow centered marketing column.
+- Exact width, aspect-fit treatment, action row arrangement and prior-result placement during rerender are open design details.
+
+### Phone
+
+- Use the shared compact phone navigation and no persistent sidebar.
+- Stack heading/status, stage, playback/progress and actions in semantic order with no page-level horizontal scrolling.
+- Preserve portrait, landscape and square source orientation inside the stage without cropping or forcing a fixed decorative ratio.
+- Controls used during playback and recovery have at least a 44px touch target.
+- The main action for the current state appears without requiring horizontal action scrolling. Secondary actions may wrap or stack while retaining their labels.
+- System browser backgrounding does not imply render cancellation. On resume, refresh authoritative status.
+- Sharing's phone presentation belongs to the sharing-dialog owner; Result only invokes it and restores focus when it closes.
+
+### Keyboard and assistive technology
+
+- Heading, status, stage/player, progress/recovery and actions follow the same logical DOM and focus order as the visual reading order.
+- All player, download, retry, share and return actions are keyboard operable with visible focus on both light surfaces and the black stage.
+- Assembly state changes use a restrained live region. Frequent progress updates must not repeatedly interrupt the user; terminal ready/failed/stale outcomes are announced once.
+- A determinate progress control exposes its value and label; an indeterminate state is named without a fabricated percentage.
+- Current, previous and outdated result status is conveyed in text, not color alone.
+- Disabled actions expose the reason through adjacent text or an accessible description rather than a hover-only tooltip.
+- Video has an accessible name and standard time controls. No subtitle control is promised when the product has added no subtitles.
+- Reduced-motion preference removes decorative transition only. It does not remove progress, player position or state feedback.
+- After the sharing dialog closes, focus returns to its invoker. After a successful retry transitions into progress, focus remains stable unless a blocking error requires focused guidance.
+
+## 13. Visible language and localization
+
+The interface supports English and Russian. Project titles and user content may mix Cyrillic and Latin scripts. System copy uses sentence case, plain verbs and one name per action through pending, success and failure states.
+
+Confirmed action concepts are:
+
+- Download;
+- Share;
+- Return to turns;
+- Retry, when the selected recovery policy permits it.
+
+The interface must communicate these facts when applicable:
+
+- the result is being assembled or validated;
+- accepted recordings remain saved;
+- a previous finished result remains available and is not the new version;
+- current project work needs one or more compatible recordings;
+- assembly failed and whether retry is available;
+- download failed without invalidating the result;
+- a result is ready and is the current generation.
+
+Exact English/Russian labels, progress stage wording, error text and previous/outdated terminology are **OPEN-10-06**. Working translations in a prototype or mock are placeholders and cannot be treated as approved copy. Internal terms such as generation fence, blob, worker, callback, codec or object storage do not appear in user-facing messages.
